answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost. A wharf stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a copper holds the rep...
